clue.text: Unbelievable! Spooner's cutting the grass without looking

indicators.note: Dr Spooner was famous for swapping the opening sounds of two words, so the starts of a pair change places

blocks.note: without looking is blind; it takes its partner's opening sound
cutting the grass is mowing; it takes its partner's opening sound

explanation.surface: Someone marvels that a man named Spooner is mowing his lawn with his eyes shut.
explanation.walkthrough: Blind mowing, with its first sounds swapped, becomes MIND-BLOWING.
explanation.definitionFit: Something mind-blowing is so astonishing it seems beyond belief, a close informal synonym used as an exclamation.

clue.text: Market's opening early before eggs land

indicators.note: an opening is where something starts, so only the first letter is wanted

blocks.note: the first letter of market
early times are old ones, as in the early or old masters
ova is the Latin plural for eggs

explanation.surface: A market opens at dawn before egg deliveries arrive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Land' looks like a verb about eggs arriving, but it is the definition, a country.
explanation.definitionFit: Moldova is an Eastern European country lying between Romania and Ukraine, so it is a land.

clue.text: Standard of Spain or Malta

indicators.note: something taken from inside the following words is made of part of them

blocks.note: runs across the end of Spain, the whole of or, and the start of Malta

explanation.surface: Someone asks what counts as the usual practice in Spain or in Malta.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits in plain view across 'SpaiN OR MALta'.
explanation.definitionFit: Normal and standard are adjective synonyms for the usual, typical or expected condition of things.

clue.text: Discusses sportspeople on a circuit

blocks.note: in cricket a batsman is often called a bat
taken as written
a circuit of a course or track is a round

explanation.surface: A commentator talks about athletes lapping a racetrack.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' places one piece after another. Bat is cricket shorthand for a batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: To bat an idea around is an idiom meaning to talk it over casually and consider it from several sides.

clue.text: Private Confederate officer said is just

indicators.note: what is said is spoken, so the words count for their sound rather than their spelling

blocks.note: private means one's own, and Robert E. Lee was the leading Confederate general in the American Civil War

explanation.surface: A soldier of the Confederacy is described as a fair-minded officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Private' looks like a military rank beside 'officer', but it means personal, one's own.
explanation.definitionFit: As adverbs, just and only both mean merely or no more than, as in only a minute.

clue.text: Approaching one mile in underground tunnel, not hollowed out

indicators.note: a thing hollowed out has lost its insides, leaving only its outer shell

blocks.note: Roman numeral one
standard abbreviation for mile
a mine is a network of tunnels dug underground
the outside letters of not

explanation.surface: Someone is about a mile into an underground tunnel that has not yet been fully dug out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' only links the pieces here; nothing goes inside anything.
explanation.definitionFit: Something imminent is about to happen, close at hand in time, so it is approaching.

clue.text: Italian's refusal to feed birds

indicators.note: food goes into whatever is fed, so one piece is put inside another

blocks.note: the word of refusal
geese are birds

explanation.surface: An Italian refuses to feed the birds, perhaps pigeons in a piazza.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is short for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A Genoese is a native of Genoa, the port city in north-west Italy, so is one particular kind of Italian.

clue.text: Miscreant from prison with missing relative in sect

indicators.note: what is missing has been taken away, so one piece loses some letters
to be in something is to sit inside it

blocks.note: taken as written
a son is a relative
a cult is a sect

explanation.surface: A wrongdoer has escaped from prison and is hiding inside a sect, his relative now absent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From prison' reads as escaping jail, but it is the source word to be trimmed; 'relative' is the family member taken out of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A culprit is the person guilty of an offence, and a miscreant is a wrongdoer, so the nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Wine barrel emptied in inn, chance for recycling?

indicators.note: an emptied container keeps only its outside, so the outer letters remain
to be in something is to sit inside it
recycled material is broken down and made into something new, so the letters are reworked

blocks.note: the first and last letters of barrel
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An empty wine barrel at a pub might be a chance for some recycling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barrel' looks like part of the wine picture, but only its shell is used; 'inn' and 'chance' are shuffled together around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Chenin blanc is a white grape variety and the white wine made from it, typical of the Loire valley.

clue.text: Such plates bistro ordered might show abnormalities

indicators.note: putting things in order means rearranging them from how they arrived
the longer word is what the combination could produce, so working backwards one part has to be taken out of it

blocks.note: so means such, as in so many
surface padding, setting the scene for plates being ordered
anomalies are abnormalities

explanation.surface: Plates ordered by a bistro might turn up chipped or misshapen.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the answer plus SO rearranges into ANOMALIES, so take SO out of ANOMALIES and rearrange the rest. 'Bistro' only dresses the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Laminae are thin layers or plates, especially of bone or rock, the Latin plural used in biology and geology.

clue.text: Tribal adviser and fine subordinate blossom

blocks.note: an elder is a senior member who advises a tribe
F for fine, as on pencil grades
lower in rank is subordinate

explanation.surface: A tribe's wise counsellor and a decent junior both flourish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blossom' reads as a verb for the two people thriving, but it is the noun being defined.
explanation.definitionFit: Elderflower is the creamy white flower of the elder tree, so it is a kind of blossom.

clue.text: Aircraft bringing individual back with delay? Indeed

indicators.note: going back means running the opposite way, so the letters are read in reverse

blocks.note: one individual is a single one
a lag is a delay
ay is an old form of yes, indeed

explanation.surface: A plane is bringing someone home late, and the speaker confirms it.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a specific aircraft named by its pilot after his mother.
explanation.definitionFit: The Enola Gay was the American B-29 bomber that dropped the atomic bomb on Hiroshima in 1945.

clue.text: Mean after all's said and done in Yorkshire?

indicators.note: Yorkshire speech famously clips its articles down to a single consonant, cutting letters out

blocks.note: a phrase meaning ultimately; in Yorkshire dialect the article is shortened to t'

explanation.surface: Someone asks what something means once everything has been talked through in Yorkshire.
explanation.walkthrough: Yorkshire speech shortens 'the' to t', so the phrase becomes 'in t'end'.
explanation.definitionFit: To mean to do something is to intend it, so the two verbs are synonyms for having a purpose.

clue.text: Remorseless training inept men to accept Information Technology

indicators.note: training knocks raw material into a new shape, so the letters are reorganised
to accept something is to take it in, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: taken as written
IT is the abbreviation for information technology

explanation.surface: A merciless trainer is forcing incompetent staff to embrace computing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remorseless' looks like it describes the training, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An impenitent person feels no regret for wrongdoing, which is exactly what being without remorse means.

clue.text: Slavic fellow removing daughter from bed

indicators.note: removing something takes it away, so letters are dropped

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for daughter
a divan is a type of bed

explanation.surface: A Russian man moves his daughter out of a bed.
explanation.walkthrough: DIVAN without its D leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivan is a common Russian and Slavic man's name, the equivalent of John, so it fits a typical Slavic man.

clue.text: Take control of company browser to follow 1,000 staff

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for company
Roman numeral for a thousand
to staff a post is to man it
deer browse, nibbling leaves and shoots

explanation.surface: A business takes over a web browser product after hiring a thousand staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Browser' suggests web software, but here it is an animal that grazes on shrubs; it comes after the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To commandeer is to seize something for one's own use, especially by authority, so it means taking control.

clue.text: Shocked when fish tail from bin's found in drink

indicators.note: a tail is the very end, so only the final letter is taken
what is found in something lies inside it

blocks.note: a hake is a fish
the final letter of bin
a sup is a sip or drink

explanation.surface: Someone is horrified to find a fish tail from the bin floating in their drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tail' looks like part of the fish, but it takes the end of the bin.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaken up is a phrasal idiom for upset or rattled, the state of someone who has had a shock.

clue.text: Heard shaggy-haired beast and Solo act half-heartedly without weapons

indicators.note: what is heard reaches the ear, so the sound counts, not the spelling
losing half of the heart means dropping one of the two central letters

blocks.note: a bear is a shaggy beast
Han Solo is the smuggler in Star Wars
an act is a deed

explanation.surface: A shaggy beast and a Star Wars hero are listened to performing a lacklustre unarmed act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solo' looks like a solo performance, but it points to Han Solo. DEED loses one of its middle Es.
explanation.definitionFit: Fighting barehanded means using bare hands and nothing else, so being without weapons of any kind.

clue.text: Long boards behind fitter

indicators.note: to board a vessel is to get on and inside it

blocks.note: the rear is the behind
to be dying for something is to long for it

explanation.surface: Long planks are fixed at the back by a tradesman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fitter' reads as a tradesman, but it is the comparative of fit, meaning more prepared.
explanation.definitionFit: Fit can mean suitable or prepared, as in fit to go, so fitter means more prepared or readier.

clue.text: Work with aluminium and stone

blocks.note: op is short for opus, a work
Al is the chemical symbol for aluminium

explanation.surface: A craftsman works with metal and stone.
explanation.walkthrough: Op is the abbreviation for opus, a numbered musical work.
explanation.definitionFit: Opal is an iridescent gemstone, so it is an example of a precious stone.

clue.text: Splendid residences friend serves well

blocks.note: a pal is a friend
in tennis a server who aces delivers an unreturnable serve

explanation.surface: A friend works as a capable servant in grand houses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Serves well' looks like domestic service, but it is tennis.
explanation.definitionFit: Palaces are grand official homes of royalty or bishops, so they are magnificent residences.

clue.text: Revolutionary sent gold to the north

indicators.note: in a down entry heading north means going upward, against the reading direction

blocks.note: to cast is to throw or send
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A rebel dispatched gold northwards.
explanation.walkthrough: Or is the heraldic word for gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Fidel Castro led the Cuban Revolution of 1959, so he is the archetypal modern revolutionary.

clue.text: That's woeful overlapping music style somewhere in America

indicators.note: overlapping pieces share a letter where they meet rather than simply joining

blocks.note: alas is a cry of woe; its final S is shared with the next piece
ska is a Jamaican music style

explanation.surface: Someone laments a dreadful musical genre heard somewhere in the US.
explanation.walkthrough: ALAS and SKA share their S, so it is written once.
explanation.definitionFit: Alaska is the largest US state, in the far north-west of North America, so it is a place in America.

clue.text: Reject papers turned yellowish

indicators.note: something turned faces the other way, so its letters run backwards

blocks.note: ID papers are identity documents
sallow skin has a sickly yellowish tinge

explanation.surface: Old documents are thrown out because they have gone yellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned yellowish' reads as ageing paper; 'turned' acts only on the papers.
explanation.definitionFit: To disallow is to refuse to accept, as a referee disallows a goal, so it is a synonym of reject.

clue.text: Modify belief that disregards the King

indicators.note: disregarding something leaves it out of account, so letters are dropped

blocks.note: to give credit to a story is to believe it
CR is Carolus Rex, Latin for King Charles

explanation.surface: Someone changes a doctrine so that it ignores the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: CR stands for Carolus Rex; strip it from the front of CREDIT.
explanation.definitionFit: To edit a text is to revise or alter it, so it is a synonym of modify.

clue.text: Unusual hindrance withdrawing gunners hit

indicators.note: withdrawing something pulls it out, so letters are taken away
unusual means out of the ordinary, so the letters are not in their normal order

blocks.note: taken as written
RA is the Royal Artillery, the British army's gunners

explanation.surface: An odd obstacle stops artillery troops from striking.
explanation.walkthrough: Take RA from HINDRANCE and rearrange what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: To chin someone is British slang for punching them on the jaw, so chinned means hit.

clue.text: One seducing gents, vices are completely without limits

indicators.note: every word loses its boundaries, so the end letters of each are stripped away

blocks.note: gents without its first and last letters
vices without its first and last letters
are without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A seducer of men has vices that know no bounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Completely' tells you to trim every one of the three words, not just the last.
explanation.definitionFit: An enticer lures or tempts others, so a person who seduces is one, a straightforward agent noun synonym.

clue.text: Concerning to Parisian, small debts unchanging

blocks.note: re means concerning, as in a letter heading
petit is French for small
IOUs are written promises of debts

explanation.surface: A Parisian is worried by a few small debts that never go away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Concerning' looks like worrying, but it is the short word re.
explanation.definitionFit: Something repetitious keeps doing the same thing over again, so it is monotonous and unchanging.
